Package org.aeonbits.owner

Class ConfigFactory

java.lang.Object
org.aeonbits.owner.ConfigFactory
public final class ConfigFactory extends Object
A static factory class to instantiate Config instances.

By default a Config sub-interface is associated to a property having the same package name and class name as the interface itself.

Method names are mapped to property names contained in the property files.

This is a singleton static class, to be used as convenience when only a single factory is needed inside an application. It exposes the newInstance() method to create new instances of Factory objects.

Author:
Luigi R. Viggiano

    • create

      public static <T extends Config> T create(Class<? extends T> clazz, Map<?,?>... imports)
      Creates a Config instance from the specified interface

      Every entry of the given imports must have a non-null String key and a non-null String value: see Factory.create(Class, Map[]) for the rationale.

      Type Parameters:
      T - type of the interface.
      Parameters:
      clazz - the interface extending from Config that you want to instantiate.
      imports - additional variables to be used to resolve the properties.
      Returns:
      an object implementing the given interface, which maps methods to property values.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if any of the imports contains a null or non-String key or value.

    • registerValueHandler

      public static void registerValueHandler(ValueHandler handler)
      Registers a handler a value can name, as ${$name::payload}, instead of holding its own text.

      See Factory.registerValueHandler(ValueHandler). Registering is the only way a handler gets in - there is no discovery on the classpath - and a configuration keeps the handlers registered when it was created, so this comes before create(Class, Map[]).

      Parameters:
      handler - the handler to register.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the handler is null, or its name is null, empty or contains whitespace or any of $ : { }.
      Since:
      2.0.0

    • setTypeConverter

      public static void setTypeConverter(Class<?> type, Class<? extends Converter<?>> converter)
      Sets a converter for the given type. Setting a converter via this method will override any default converters but not Config.ConverterClass annotations.

      Like every static method here, this one is the default factory and nothing more: it sets the converter for the configurations created through create(Class, Map[]) and not for those created by a factory of your own, which since 2.0.0 keeps its own converters. See Factory.setTypeConverter(java.lang.Class<?>, java.lang.Class<? extends org.aeonbits.owner.Converter<?>>).

      Parameters:
      type - the type for which to set a converter.
      converter - the converter class to use for the specified type.
      Since:
      1.0.10
